a new method was established to determine and analyze arsenic speciation, which can be applied to the pharmacokinetics study of arsenic speciations in traditional Chinese medicine.

a new method was developed for the determination of inorganic arsenic, arsenobetaine, and dimethylarsinic acid, and the pharmacokinetic profiles of arsenic speciations after oral administration of Xiao-Er-Zhao-Ban-Wan were determined.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and validation of a new method of high performance ion chromatography with inductive coupled plasma mass spectrometer for the simultaneous determination of arsenic species in traditional Chinese medicines.
the determination and pharmacokinetics of the arsenic species in Xiao-Er-Bao-Wan.
the determination of arsenical speciation in traditional Chinese medicines and the pharmacokinetic properties after oral administration in a rat model.

, after oral dosing, the plasma concentration-time curve of As(III), As(V) and dimethylarsenic acid was obtained.

, in the Xiao-Er-Zhao-Bao-Wan pills, arsenic exists mainly as As(V), and the average concentration of arsenic is 10105.5 ± 380.8 mg/kg, with the inorganic As(V) and As(III) concentrations being 220.1 and 45.4 mg/kg, respectively, in the water extraction solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for the determination of the speciation of arsenic in the pills and water extracts.

, after oral intake of Xiao-Er-Zheng-Bao-Wan pills, the plasma concentrations of As(V), dimethyl arsenic, and As(III) peaked at 0.5 h (Cmax) and reached 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 μg/mL, respectively, and the half-life (t1/2) of As(V), Dimethyl arsenic, As(III) were 3.5 ± 1.

we have successfully developed a simple, rapid, sensitive, and selective analytical method for the determination of As(III), As(V), and dimethylarsenic acid in the plasma of rats after oral administration of Xiao-Er-Zh-Bao-Wan, which could provide a reference for the determination of other arsenic-containing medicines and could also be used to evaluate the toxicity of arsenic in traditional medicines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, after oral dosing, As(III), As(V), and dimethylarsinic acid are the main arsenic species in the plasma of the rats, and that the pharmacokinetics properties are different for each of the arsenic species.
the pharmacokinetic properties and toxicity of As(V) and As(III) are different.
, in traditional Chinese medicine, arsenic is present in the form of arsenic acid, which can be easily absorbed by the human body and is highly toxic.
